question: What is the main focus of competency-based midwifery education?

options.A: Passing written examinations without practical tests
options.B: Demonstrating specific, measurable clinical skills
options.C: Memorising the history of global nursing leaders
options.D: Completing a fixed number of hours sitting in lectures

explanation: Competency-based education prioritises the actual performance and mastery of practical tasks over time spent in a classroom. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T3#BMP312_U3_T3_h2)

question: What is the main purpose of hospital management structures?

options.A: Increasing the cost of specialized treatments
options.B: Ensuring safe care and accountability
options.C: Replacing the need for direct ward management
options.D: Preventing nurses from making clinical choices

explanation: Clear lines of authority help maintain order, legal compliance, and safe practices across all departments. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T1#BMP110_U2_T1_h1)

question: What happens in blood vessels when nifedipine blocks calcium entry?

options.A: The blood flow stops completely
options.B: The vessel walls become thickened
options.C: The blood vessels dilate and relax
options.D: The blood vessels constrict tightly

explanation: Stopping calcium from entering muscle cells keeps them from squeezing, causing blood vessels to open up and lower pressure. [learn more](BMP213_U3_T4#BMP213_U3_T4_h2)

question: How can facilities best address poor data quality caused by rushed documentation?

options.A: Punish midwives by withholding their salaries when mistakes happen
options.B: Stop submitting monthly reports until the government builds new offices
options.C: Abolish all registers and rely entirely on patient memory for history
options.D: Conduct routine data quality audits and train staff on proper record keeping

explanation: Supportive supervision, regular audits, and continuous training improve accuracy much more effectively than punitive measures. [learn more](BMP123_U5_T1#BMP123_U5_T1_h6)

question: Which substance must patients with active hepatitis strictly avoid to prevent worsening liver injury?

options.A: Alcohol
options.B: Filtered water
options.C: Complex carbohydrates
options.D: Fresh fruits

explanation: Alcohol is metabolized by the liver and adds toxic stress to an already inflamed and struggling organ, accelerating tissue damage. [learn more](BMP125_U4_T1#BMP125_U4_T1_h5)

question: Which of the following actions is NOT recommended when preparing a wide multi-column table for physical printing?

options.A: Adjusting column widths to prevent data cutoff
options.B: Checking the layout using the print preview tool
options.C: Switching the page layout to landscape orientation
options.D: Keeping the page layout in portrait orientation

explanation: Wide tables with many columns will get cut off horizontally in portrait orientation and usually require landscape mode. [learn more](BMP123_U3_T2#BMP123_U3_T2_h7)

question: When is the best time for the first routine clinic check-up after an uncomplicated IUCD insertion?

options.A: After exactly one full year of continuous use
options.B: After the first spontaneous menses or 4 to 6 weeks
options.C: Only when the client decides to become pregnant
options.D: Within twenty-four hours of leaving the clinic

explanation: A follow-up visit at 4 to 6 weeks or after the first period helps confirm that the IUCD is in place and that the client is adjusting well. [learn more](BMP224_U3_T9#BMP224_U3_T9_h4)

question: Why does severe hypothyroidism cause a thick swelling under the skin called myxedema?

options.A: Severe protein deficiency from poor nutritional intake
options.B: Excessive fluid retention caused by primary kidney failure
options.C: An accumulation of mucopolysaccharides in the skin tissues
options.D: A blockage of the lymphatic vessels in the lower limbs

explanation: Special sugar-protein molecules build up under the skin in severe cases, trapping water and causing that thick, non-pitting swelling. [learn more](BMP216_U2_T6#BMP216_U2_T6_h1)

question: Which everyday activity connects patient care directly to a maternity unit's financial costs?

options.A: Writing hospital policies for public health programs
options.B: Conducting research on rare obstetric complications
options.C: Designing architectural layouts for new delivery suites
options.D: Scheduling staff shifts and requesting consumables

explanation: Daily tasks like using supplies and organizing shift rosters directly consume the unit's financial resources. [learn more](BMP312_U2_T3#BMP312_U2_T3_h1)

question: Which tissue layer inside a joint is primarily affected during rheumatoid arthritis?

options.A: Articular cartilage
options.B: Compact bone shaft
options.C: Skeletal muscle belly
options.D: Synovial membrane

explanation: Rheumatoid arthritis is an autoimmune condition that specifically targets the synovium, causing inflammation and the growth of destructive tissue known as a pannus. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T6#BMP216_U3_T6_h1)

question: What is the main function of gap junctions in body tissues?

options.A: Anchoring the bottom of the cell to the basement membrane
options.B: Allowing direct chemical communication between cells
options.C: Creating a waterproof seal to block fluid movement
options.D: Locking cells tightly together during heavy stretching

explanation: Gap junctions create small channels that let ions and small molecules pass directly from the cytoplasm of one cell to the next. [learn more](BMP111_U1_T6#BMP111_U1_T6_h2)

question: Why do liver enzymes become elevated in HELLP syndrome?

options.A: Fibrin deposits block blood flow in the liver and cause tissue damage
options.B: Excessive red blood cell production overworks the liver
options.C: High maternal blood pressure directly destroys liver cells
options.D: The kidneys stop filtering bile acids properly into the urine

explanation: Tiny clots and fibrin deposits in the liver spaces obstruct circulation, causing liver cell injury and enzyme leakage. [learn more](BMP221_U3_T6#BMP221_U3_T6_h1)

question: Why is an intestinal obstruction considered a medical emergency?

options.A: It immediately stops the kidneys from producing urine
options.B: It always spreads contagious bacteria to other patients
options.C: It permanently cures chronic high blood pressure
options.D: It quickly causes severe fluid loss and tissue death

explanation: Trapped contents and pressure can cut off blood supply to the bowel, causing tissue to die very quickly. [learn more](BMP125_U3_T9#BMP125_U3_T9_h1)

question: In the ABCDE primary survey framework, what does the letter 'C' stand for?

options.A: Coughing
options.B: Circulation
options.C: Contraction
options.D: Coma

explanation: In emergency assessment, C stands for circulation, checking pulses, bleeding, and perfusion. [learn more](BMP110_U7_T1#BMP110_U7_T1_h4)

question: What is the main reason for drying a newborn right after birth?

options.A: To prevent heat loss and hypothermia
options.B: To remove all the vernix caseosa from the skin
options.C: To help the heart blood vessel close properly
options.D: To check for skin birthmarks

explanation: Wet skin leads to rapid evaporative heat loss, making immediate drying essential to protect the newborn from cold stress. [learn more](BMP215_U2_T3#BMP215_U2_T3_h6)

question: Why is the stoma site marked while the patient is in different positions like sitting and standing?

options.A: To test the strength of the abdominal muscles
options.B: To measure the exact length of the bowel
options.C: To determine how much fluid the patient needs
options.D: To avoid skin folds and the beltline

explanation: Marking the site in various postures ensures the pouch stays secure and does not wrinkle or leak when the patient moves. [learn more](BMP125_U3_T12#BMP125_U3_T12_h2)

question: A patient who was admitted voluntarily last week now demands to leave immediately, but nurses notice severe active psychosis with suicidal intent. What is the most appropriate initial nursing action?

options.A: Assess the patient's current safety risk and evaluate criteria for involuntary conversion
options.B: Call security immediately to physically force the patient to stay in bed
options.C: Discharge the patient right away since voluntary status grants unconditional leaving
options.D: Ignore the request to leave until the attending doctor returns next week

explanation: When a voluntary patient poses a risk to self or others, staff must evaluate whether to transition them to involuntary status for safety. [learn more](BMP223_U1_T4#BMP223_U1_T4_h2)

question: When a midwife measures the diagonal conjugate during an examination, what is she trying to estimate indirectly?

options.A: The outlet anteroposterior diameter
options.B: The bisischial diameter
options.C: The transverse inlet diameter
options.D: The obstetric conjugate

explanation: The diagonal conjugate is measured with fingers to estimate the true obstetric conjugate, which cannot be reached directly. [learn more](BMP210_U1_T2#BMP210_U1_T2_h2)

question: Why are interactive case studies and simulations preferred over long lectures for midwifery students?

options.A: They make it easier for the tutor to avoid preparing lesson plans
options.B: They allow students to actively solve problems they will face in the ward
options.C: They guarantee that students will never make mistakes in clinical practice
options.D: They completely eliminate the need for studying textbooks or guidelines

explanation: Active methods match the adult learner's need for practical, problem-centered education that prepares them for real-life clinical duties. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T1#BMP312_U3_T1_h6)

question: Which of these layers is NOT part of the early placental membrane in the first trimester?

options.A: Fetal capillary endothelium
options.B: Syncytiotrophoblast layer
options.C: Villous connective tissue
options.D: Myometrial smooth muscle layer

explanation: The myometrium is part of the mother's uterine wall, whereas the placental membrane consists only of trophoblastic and fetal vascular layers. [learn more](BMP210_U5_T1#BMP210_U5_T1_h4)

question: What is the main benefit of applying a cold pack to the perineum within the first 24 hours?

options.A: Preventing the lochia flow completely
options.B: Stimulating early breast milk production
options.C: Speeding up the dissolving of stitches
options.D: Reducing swelling and numbing pain

explanation: Cold therapy narrows blood vessels, which helps decrease swelling and provides a mild numbing effect on nerve endings. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T6#BMP218_U2_T6_h5)

question: Which medication is currently given to prevent malaria during pregnancy in Nigeria?

options.A: Artemether-Lumefantrine
options.B: Chloroquine phosphate
options.C: Sulfadoxine-Pyrimethamine
options.D: Intravenous Quinine

explanation: Sulfadoxine-Pyrimethamine (SP) is the recommended medicine for Intermittent Preventive Treatment during pregnancy at scheduled antenatal visits. [learn more](BMP116_U3_T4#BMP116_U3_T4_h7)

question: What happens if an instrument is not cleaned thoroughly before going into the autoclave?

options.A: The metallic surface becomes completely immune to future rusting
options.B: Remaining organic matter bakes onto the metal and blocks sterilization
options.C: The autoclave machine will increase its internal pressure to compensate
options.D: The instrument automatically changes its chemical color to bright red

explanation: Blood and tissue left on dirty tools harden during heating, protecting trapped germs from the steam. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T1#BMP110_U4_T1_h3)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common side effect of morphine for the mother?

options.A: Persistent tachycardia
options.B: Delayed gastric emptying
options.C: Nausea and vomiting
options.D: Excessive drowsiness

explanation: Morphine typically causes sedation and respiratory suppression rather than persistent high heart rates (tachycardia). [learn more](BMP213_U2_T2#BMP213_U2_T2_h4)

question: What is the main goal of a birth debriefing session led by a midwife?

options.A: Providing a safe space for the mother to narrate her labor story
options.B: Conducting a full neurological examination of the newborn infant
options.C: Calculating the precise financial cost of hospital admission
options.D: Administering intravenous prophylactic antibiotics for infection

explanation: Birth debriefing gives mothers a chance to process their experiences, ask questions, and make sense of their labor. [learn more](BMP223_U2_T4#BMP223_U2_T4_h6)

question: What does a high p-value above 0.05 actually mean for a tested intervention?

options.A: The treatment is proven to be dangerous for mothers
options.B: The research participants lied on their questionnaires
options.C: The study lacked enough evidence to prove an effect
options.D: The medical equipment used was completely broken

explanation: A non-significant p-value means we cannot rule out chance, not that we have definitive proof the treatment does nothing. [learn more](BMP225_U4_T4#BMP225_U4_T4_h4)

question: Why is diagnosing superimposed preeclampsia often challenging in clinical practice?

options.A: Symptoms never appear until after the baby is delivered
options.B: The patient often already has high blood pressure and baseline protein in her urine
options.C: Laboratory tests are completely normal in these patients
options.D: Blood pressure readings usually drop to normal during the second trimester

explanation: Because chronic high blood pressure and baseline kidney issues may already cause elevated readings and protein, spotting new changes takes extra clinical care. [learn more](BMP221_U3_T1#BMP221_U3_T1_h7)

question: When should you document a nursing intervention that you just performed?

options.A: Only when the patient requests a medical report
options.B: At the end of the entire working week
options.C: Before the doctor comes around for morning ward round
options.D: Promptly after completing the care intervention

explanation: Documentation should be done immediately after care to prevent memory lapses and ensure accuracy. [learn more](BMP120_U1_T5#BMP120_U1_T5_h5)

question: Why is it helpful for a midwife to ask a menopausal patient about her daily routine and work environment?

options.A: To decide if she needs surgery on her reproductive organs
options.B: To calculate her monthly income for hospital records
options.C: To identify personal triggers that worsen her hot flashes
options.D: To prove whether she is experiencing true menopause

explanation: Knowing a patient's daily routine helps pinpoint environmental and dietary triggers that can be adjusted to reduce hot flashes. [learn more](BMP320_U1_T2#BMP320_U1_T2_h5)

question: What is a major risk associated with general anaesthesia in pregnant women?

options.A: Permanent loss of the mother's sense of hearing
options.B: Instantaneous weight gain in the immediate postpartum period
options.C: Complete absence of any uterine contractions ever again
options.D: Rapid development of maternal oxygen shortage

explanation: Pregnant women have reduced oxygen reserves in their lungs, causing them to run out of oxygen quickly when unconscious. [learn more](BMP124_U3_T5#BMP124_U3_T5_h3)

question: A midwife continues to manage patients in a rural maternity clinic even though her practicing license expired six months ago. What is the status of this practice?

options.A: It is valid provided she pays her renewal fees by the end of the year
options.B: It is permitted if the local community leaders approve her work
options.C: It is acceptable as long as she completed her initial training
options.D: It is illegal and constitutes professional malpractice

explanation: Practicing without a current, valid license violates the NMCN Act and renders the practice illegal, regardless of past qualifications. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T4#BMP211_U1_T4_h4)

question: How is uterine tachysystole defined during labor induction monitoring?

options.A: Contractions lasting continuously for over fifteen minutes without a break
options.B: Fewer than two contractions in a full twenty-minute observation window
options.C: More than five contractions in ten minutes averaged over thirty minutes
options.D: Painful uterine cramping that occurs only once every hour during the night

explanation: Tachysystole means having too many contractions in a short time, which can lower blood flow to the placenta and stress the baby. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T8#BMP213_U1_T8_h8)

question: Which symptom requires immediate investigation for a potential pulmonary embolism in a pregnant woman?

options.A: A dry nighttime cough from a mild cold
options.B: Seasonal sneezing due to pollen allergies
options.C: Mild fatigue after climbing one flight of stairs
options.D: Sharp chest pain linked to breathing

explanation: Pleuritic chest pain combined with sudden breathlessness is a classic warning sign of a blood clot in the lungs. [learn more](BMP125_U1_T1#BMP125_U1_T1_h2)

question: What should you expect to see in the water seal chamber during normal patient breathing?

options.A: Violent, continuous bubbling that never stops
options.B: Complete stillness of the water with zero movement
options.C: Rapid evaporation of all the fluid within a few hours
options.D: Tidalling, where the water level moves up and down with breathing

explanation: Tidalling reflects normal pressure changes in the pleural cavity as the patient breathes in and out. [learn more](BMP125_U1_T11#BMP125_U1_T11_h3)

question: What is the correct minimum time interval between the first and second dose of tetanus toxoid?

options.A: Exactly 1 week apart
options.B: At least 6 months apart
options.C: At least 4 weeks apart
options.D: Exactly 24 hours apart

explanation: TT2 must be administered a minimum of four weeks following the initial TT1 dose to properly build up maternal immunity. [learn more](BMP218_U1_T3#BMP218_U1_T3_h3)

question: What is the primary underlying problem in all forms of shock?

options.A: Complete failure of the central nervous system
options.B: Inadequate tissue perfusion and cellular oxygenation
options.C: Severe elevation in systemic arterial blood pressure
options.D: Sudden and permanent cessation of heart sounds

explanation: Shock fundamentally represents a failure of the circulatory system to supply tissues with enough oxygen and nutrients for normal function. [learn more](BMP110_U7_T4#BMP110_U7_T4_h1)

question: When organizing clinic supplies, what should be done with contraceptives nearing their expiry date?

options.A: Throw them immediately into the municipal waste bin
options.B: Donate them directly to clients outside the clinic
options.C: Dispense them using the first-in, first-out rule
options.D: Move them to the back of the shelf out of reach

explanation: The first-in, first-out inventory rule ensures older stock is used before it expires, reducing wastage. [learn more](BMP224_U1_T4#BMP224_U1_T4_h2)

question: Why does a lack of social support significantly increase a new mother's risk for developing postpartum depression?

options.A: It leaves her isolated to carry the heavy physical and emotional burden of childcare alone.
options.B: It prevents her body from producing enough breast milk for the baby.
options.C: It forces her blood pressure to rise to dangerously high levels.
options.D: It automatically causes an immediate infection in the uterine lining.

explanation: Isolation and lack of practical help compound the exhaustion of new motherhood, creating a fertile ground for overwhelming stress and depression. [learn more](BMP223_U3_T1#BMP223_U3_T1_h3)

question: What shape describes the pelvic inlet of an android pelvis?

options.A: Oval-shaped
options.B: Uniformly round
options.C: Heart-shaped
options.D: Transverse-shaped

explanation: The promontory of the sacrum and the converging side walls push inward, creating a characteristic wedge or heart shape at the inlet. [learn more](BMP210_U1_T4#BMP210_U1_T4_h2)

question: What usually happens when an ultra-rapid metabolizer takes a standard dose of a medicine?

options.A: Severe toxicity from immediate drug accumulation
options.B: Therapeutic failure because the drug is cleared too quickly
options.C: Total blockage of gastrointestinal absorption
options.D: Permanent deactivation of liver enzymes

explanation: If enzymes process a medicine too fast, blood levels drop before the drug has a chance to help the patient. [learn more](BMP124_U1_T6#BMP124_U1_T6_h4)

question: A pregnant woman at 34 weeks has a severe headache, blurry vision, and sudden convulsions. Which nervous system complication is she most likely experiencing?

options.A: Hyperemesis gravidarum
options.B: Eclampsia
options.C: Normal labor pains
options.D: Gestational diabetes

explanation: Sudden seizures or convulsions in a pregnant woman with signs of pre-eclampsia point to eclampsia, a serious nervous system emergency. [learn more](BMP121_U5_T2#BMP121_U5_T2_h7)

question: Why is keeping a bleeding patient warm during transport so important?

options.A: Patients in shock always have a fever
options.B: Hypothermia worsens blood clotting problems
options.C: Warm blankets restore lost red blood cells
options.D: Heat stops the heart from beating too fast

explanation: Cold body temperatures interfere with the body's natural ability to form clots and stop bleeding. [learn more](BMP110_U7_T3#BMP110_U7_T3_h6)

question: Why are the negative symptoms of schizophrenia often difficult to treat in clinical practice?

options.A: They cause violent outbursts that require immediate physical restraint
options.B: They disappear completely within forty-eight hours without any medical help
options.C: They poorly respond to typical antipsychotic drugs and reduce daily functioning
options.D: They only appear during nighttime hours and do not affect daytime nursing care

explanation: Negative symptoms like withdrawal and lack of energy do not respond as well to medication as hallucinations do. [learn more](BMP223_U3_T3#BMP223_U3_T3_h3)

question: Which immune cells are the main target of the Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV)?

options.A: Platelets
options.B: CD4+ T-lymphocytes
options.C: Red blood cells
options.D: Neutrophils

explanation: HIV specifically targets and destroys CD4+ T-lymphocytes, which progressively weakens the body's immune defenses. [learn more](BMP116_U4_T4#BMP116_U4_T4_h1)

question: What should a midwife do immediately before leaving the computer terminal to attend to a patient in labor?

options.A: Shut down the main electrical generator for the clinic
options.B: Lock the computer screen to prevent unauthorized viewing
options.C: Unplug the central processing unit from the wall socket
options.D: Delete all open patient files from the desktop

explanation: Locking the screen ensures that confidential patient information remains protected while the workstation is unattended. [learn more](BMP123_U2_T4#BMP123_U2_T4_h5)

question: What is the main limit of measuring community health outreach success by head count alone?

options.A: It does not measure actual knowledge retention or behavioral change
options.B: It requires too much paperwork for the ministry of health
options.C: It costs too much money to count people at the market
options.D: It prevents midwives from visiting more villages

explanation: A large crowd does not guarantee that people understood the message or will change their health practices. [learn more](BMP227_U2_T2#BMP227_U2_T2_h6)

question: What is the best way to tell if a community health mobilization program has truly worked?

options.A: The volume of medical textbooks stored in the health center office
options.B: The frequency of meetings held by foreign donor agencies
options.C: Sustainable changes in health behaviors and increased facility utilization
options.D: The total number of educational posters printed and distributed

explanation: Real success shows up when people actually change their health habits and keep using the clinic services. [learn more](BMP117_U2_T3#BMP117_U2_T3_h6)

question: What is the correct way to break the baby's suction before taking them off the breast?

options.A: Squeeze the entire breast firmly until the baby lets go
options.B: Wait until the baby falls asleep and drops off
options.C: Insert a clean finger into the corner of the baby's mouth
options.D: Pull the baby's head gently backward by the ears

explanation: Breaking the seal with a finger prevents the suction from stretching and tearing the nipple skin. [learn more](BMP214_U3_T5#BMP214_U3_T5_h4)

question: What pattern seen under a microscope confirms the presence of amniotic fluid in a fern test?

options.A: Long, thread-like fungal strands
options.B: Circular clusters of red blood cells
options.C: Clusters of oval skin cells
options.D: Crystals that look like fern leaves

explanation: When amniotic fluid dries on a glass slide, the high salt content forms a distinct fern leaf pattern under the microscope. [learn more](BMP311_U2_T1#BMP311_U2_T1_h5)

question: Which hormone is the main driver behind early cardiovascular changes in pregnancy?

options.A: Prolactin
options.B: Oxytocin
options.C: Insulin
options.D: Progesterone

explanation: Progesterone relaxes smooth muscle walls throughout the body, causing widespread vasodilation that triggers the heart to adapt early in pregnancy. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T4#BMP212_U1_T4_h1)

question: Why must the care team monitor a recovering shock patient carefully for signs of fluid overload?

options.A: Rapid fluid resuscitation can overwhelm the heart and cause fluid in the lungs
options.B: Too much fluid causes the surgical incision to heal much too quickly
options.C: Excess fluids will instantly dissolve all the circulating blood platelets
options.D: Patients who receive IV fluids always develop a permanent kidney disease

explanation: Pumping large amounts of fluid into a recovering system can back up into the lungs, causing dangerous pulmonary edema. [learn more](BMP120_U4_T5#BMP120_U4_T5_h7)

question: What name is given to the chewed mass of food ready for swallowing?

options.A: Plasma
options.B: Chyme
options.C: Feces
options.D: Bolus

explanation: Teeth and saliva work together in the mouth to shape chewed food into a smooth ball called a bolus. [learn more](BMP121_U2_T2#BMP121_U2_T2_h2)

question: Which Nigerian law provides significant legal protections against domestic and gender-based violence?

options.A: Standard Public Health Quarantine Regulation
options.B: Federal Road Safety Commission Decree
options.C: National Minimum Wage and Labor Act
options.D: Violence Against Persons Prohibition (VAPP) Act

explanation: The VAPP Act is a key legal instrument in Nigeria designed to eliminate violence in private and public life. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T4#BMP310_U1_T4_h7)

question: What is the most effective household method to kill tapeworm larvae present in raw meat?

options.A: Rinsing the meat surface with cold running water
options.B: Freezing the meat for just one hour before cooking
options.C: Cooking the meat thoroughly until no pink remains
options.D: Soaking the raw meat in vinegar for ten minutes

explanation: Heat destroys the larval cysts embedded in muscle tissue, preventing infection when the meat is consumed. [learn more](BMP116_U3_T8#BMP116_U3_T8_h7)

question: Which of the following is typically the very first sign of a developing drug allergy?

options.A: Sudden itching and skin redness
options.B: High fever with chills
options.C: Complete cardiac arrest
options.D: Severe kidney failure

explanation: Skin manifestations like itching, redness, or hives are usually the earliest physical clues that a drug is triggering an immune response. [learn more](BMP120_U2_T7#BMP120_U2_T7_h2)

question: What main feeling usually defines emotional trauma during a bad emergency?

options.A: Sudden physical numbness in the limbs
options.B: Total memory loss of the past year
options.C: Extreme physical hunger and fatigue
options.D: Intense helplessness and severe terror

explanation: Trauma can completely overwhelm a person's coping abilities, leading to deep feelings of helplessness and fear. [learn more](BMP110_U7_T10#BMP110_U7_T10_h1)

question: What primary condition is treated with mood stabilizers like lithium?

options.A: Bipolar affective disorder
options.B: Gestational diabetes mellitus
options.C: Pregnancy-induced hypertension
options.D: Iron deficiency anemia

explanation: Mood stabilizers are prescribed to help manage conditions with severe emotional swings, especially bipolar disorder. [learn more](BMP223_U4_T3#BMP223_U4_T3_h1)

question: Which of the following is NOT part of secondary prevention for cervical cancer?

options.A: Conducting routine community awareness talks
options.B: Administering chemotherapy to a patient with Stage IV disease
options.C: Screening women with a Pap smear
options.D: Performing Visual Inspection with Acetic Acid (VIA)

explanation: Giving chemotherapy to treat advanced disease is a form of treatment, whereas screening and early detection tests represent secondary prevention. [learn more](BMP320_U2_T2#BMP320_U2_T2_h6)

question: What happens when a hormone level gets too high in a standard negative feedback system?

options.A: The nervous system takes over the gland completely
options.B: The gland is stimulated to produce even more hormone
options.C: Target organs stop responding to all chemical signals
options.D: Secretion of that hormone is slowed down to lower levels

explanation: High levels of a hormone signal the body to stop releasing more, keeping amounts safe and balanced. [learn more](BMP121_U4_T3#BMP121_U4_T3_h2)

question: Why are Clostridium spores hard to get rid of on medical equipment with basic cleaning?

options.A: They actively attack cleaning staff
options.B: They dissolve standard surgical steel
options.C: They multiply rapidly in open air
options.D: They resist heat and disinfectants

explanation: Endospores have a tough outer coat that protects them against high temperatures and many standard chemical agents. [learn more](BMP116_U2_T8#BMP116_U2_T8_h2)

question: How do Streptococcus bacteria typically look under a microscope?

options.A: Single rod shapes
options.B: Chains or pairs
options.C: Spiral corkscrews
options.D: Clusters like grapes

explanation: Streptococci divide in one plane, which causes them to grow in characteristic chains or pairs under the microscope. [learn more](BMP116_U2_T4#BMP116_U2_T4_h1)

question: Why might a normal non-pregnant serum creatinine level be a warning sign during pregnancy?

options.A: Normal pregnancy lowers creatinine levels, so a standard value actually reflects reduced kidney function
options.B: Pregnancy causes the liver to produce excess creatinine which masks kidney disease
options.C: Creatinine is never measured in pregnant women because it is completely unreliable
options.D: Standard values are too low to detect normal fetal kidney waste elimination

explanation: Because healthy pregnant kidneys filter blood much faster, normal serum creatinine drops. A value in the upper normal non-pregnant range actually points to sluggish kidney function. [learn more](BMP221_U4_T10#BMP221_U4_T10_h1)

question: Where should heavy boxes of intravenous fluid cartons be stored in the ward storeroom?

options.A: Directly on open windowsills exposed to breeze

explanation: Placental abruption occurs when the placenta detaches from the uterine wall before the baby is born. [learn more](BMP221_U2_T3#BMP221_U2_T3_h1)

question: Why do midwives monitor fetal biometry measurements like femur length and abdominal circumference in the third trimester?

options.A: To detect chromosomal abnormalities like Down syndrome
options.B: To measure the strength of uterine contractions
options.C: To calculate the exact date of conception
options.D: To estimate fetal weight and check growth patterns

explanation: Biometric measurements taken later in pregnancy help healthcare providers determine if the baby is growing at a normal and healthy rate. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T6#BMP211_U2_T6_h3)

question: About how many cotyledons are usually visible on the maternal side of a full-term placenta?

options.B: 5 to 10

explanation: The maternal surface of the placenta is divided into roughly 15 to 20 distinct lobes called cotyledons. [learn more](BMP210_U5_T1#BMP210_U5_T1_h2)

question: When is the best time to give erythromycin eye ointment to a newborn?

options.A: Within the first hour following birth
options.B: Precisely twenty-four hours after delivery
options.C: Before the baby is dried and warmed
options.D: Only if signs of eye discharge appear

explanation: Giving the ointment early protects against bacteria picked up during birth before an infection can start. [learn more](BMP213_U4_T2#BMP213_U4_T2_h5)

question: Why do adolescent males typically need more calories and protein than females of the same age?

options.A: Their physical activity levels are strictly mandated by school rules
options.B: They experience menarche at a much earlier chronological age
options.C: They develop a much larger proportion of lean muscle mass and skeletal volume
options.D: Their digestive systems absorb nutrients at a much slower rate overall

explanation: The male growth spurt involves a massive increase in lean tissue and bone mass, driving up absolute energy and protein needs. [learn more](BMP118_U3_T5#BMP118_U3_T5_h4)

question: Around what gestational age is the detailed mid-pregnancy anomaly scan usually performed?

options.A: 18 to 22 weeks
options.B: 12 to 14 weeks
options.C: 6 to 8 weeks
options.D: 36 to 40 weeks

explanation: The structural anomaly scan is best performed between 18 and 22 weeks because internal organs are large enough to be clearly visualized. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T6#BMP211_U2_T6_h3)

question: Which antibiotic must be avoided when treating chlamydia in a pregnant woman?

options.A: Amoxicillin
options.B: Erythromycin
options.C: Doxycycline
options.D: Azithromycin

explanation: Doxycycline is a tetracycline antibiotic that affects fetal bone and tooth development, making it unsafe during pregnancy. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T5#BMP310_U2_T5_h5)

question: Before how many weeks of pregnancy is labor considered preterm?

options.A: Before 37 completed weeks
options.B: Before 40 completed weeks
options.C: Before 42 completed weeks
options.D: Before 32 completed weeks

explanation: Labor is classified as preterm when it happens after fetal viability is reached but before the 37th week of pregnancy is completed. [learn more](BMP311_U2_T1#BMP311_U2_T1_h1)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common challenge faced by midwife managers in many Nigerian public health facilities?

options.A: Stockouts of vital emergency obstetric drugs
options.B: Shortages of trained midwifery personnel
options.C: Excessive surplus of modern medical equipment
options.D: Erratic power supply affecting theater lights

explanation: Public health facilities in Nigeria typically suffer from equipment shortages rather than an excessive surplus, making this option the incorrect statement. [learn more](BMP312_U1_T1#BMP312_U1_T1_h6)

question: What is the standard action if the vacuum cup slips off the baby's head three times during delivery attempts?

options.A: Increase the vacuum pressure to maximum and pull harder
options.B: Wait two hours before attempting any more pulls
options.C: Switch to a metal cup and restart the entire procedure
options.D: Stop the vacuum procedure and switch to an alternative method

explanation: Repeated cup detachment means the procedure is not working properly, so it is stopped to prevent injury. [learn more](BMP311_U3_T2#BMP311_U3_T2_h5)

question: Which condition is most commonly linked to placental abruption?

options.A: Gestational gestational diabetes
options.B: Iron deficiency anaemia
options.C: Asymptomatic bacteriuria
options.D: Pregnancy-induced hypertension

explanation: High blood pressure damages the blood vessels that supply the placenta, making the tissue more likely to detach early. [learn more](BMP221_U2_T1#BMP221_U2_T1_h4)

question: What is the primary function of the ductus arteriosus during fetal life?

options.A: To divert blood away from the fluid-filled lungs into the aorta
options.B: To pump deoxygenated blood directly back into the placenta
options.C: To prevent blood from flowing backward into the heart ventricles
options.D: To supply the fetal liver with high-pressure nutrients

explanation: Since the lungs do not oxygenate blood before birth, the ductus arteriosus redirects most right ventricular output away from them. [learn more](BMP210_U5_T4#BMP210_U5_T4_h5)

question: How should a midwife best support a patient who is distressed about potential infertility caused by amenorrhea?

options.A: By focusing solely on surgical procedures without discussing her feelings
options.B: By offering empathetic listening and clear education about treatment options
options.C: By assuring her that pregnancy is guaranteed once she gains weight
options.D: By telling her that missing periods is a normal part of modern life

explanation: Holistic care requires acknowledging emotional concerns and providing accurate, reassuring information about how treating the root cause can restore health. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T1#BMP310_U3_T1_h7)

question: Why is drug treatment for intestinal parasites often delayed until after the first trimester of pregnancy?

options.A: Because parasites naturally die off on their own by week twelve
options.B: Because the maternal stomach cannot absorb drugs early on
options.C: To protect the developing fetus during major organ formation
options.D: To allow the placenta time to filter out chemical toxins

explanation: The first trimester is the critical window of organ development, making it vital to avoid medications that could harm the embryo. [learn more](BMP116_U3_T8#BMP116_U3_T8_h6)

question: Why is it important to write down the patient's exact words during a forensic assessment?

options.A: It preserves objective facts and legal integrity for potential legal proceedings
options.B: It replaces the need for a physical examination of the injuries
options.C: It guarantees that the perpetrator will be arrested within twenty-four hours
options.D: It fulfills hospital administrative filing quotas for insurance claims

explanation: Precise documentation of injuries and statements ensures reliable evidence if the survivor decides to pursue legal action. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T7#BMP310_U1_T7_h4)

question: During antenatal clinic duties, what key preventive service should a midwife promote to protect young girls against cervical cancer?

options.A: Routine chest radiography
options.B: Daily iron and folate supplementation
options.C: Prophylactic broad-spectrum antibiotics
options.D: Human Papillomavirus vaccination

explanation: Administering the HPV vaccine to young adolescent girls before sexual debut is an effective primary prevention strategy against cervical cancer. [learn more](BMP116_U4_T4#BMP116_U4_T4_h6)

question: Which blood vessels create the largest share of total resistance in the circulatory system?

options.A: Arterioles
options.B: Large veins
options.C: Venae cavae
options.D: Large elastic arteries

explanation: Arterioles provide the highest resistance in the circulatory loop, making them the main determinants of total peripheral resistance. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T14#BMP111_U5_T14_h5)

question: What is the primary role of nontreponemal tests like VDRL in clinical care?

options.A: Detecting active viral load changes in the bloodstream
options.B: Measuring exact bacterial cell counts under a microscope
options.C: Screening for infection and monitoring response to treatment
options.D: Confirming lifelong immunity after natural infection recovery

explanation: Nontreponemal tests rise and fall with disease activity, making them useful for screening and checking if treatment worked. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T6#BMP310_U2_T6_h4)

question: What is the primary cause of acute cholecystitis in most patients?

options.A: Obstruction of the cystic duct by a gallstone
options.B: Chronic inflammation of the pancreatic ducts
options.C: Bacterial infection spreading from the stomach
options.D: Excessive production of red blood cells by the spleen

explanation: Most cases happen when a hardened stone blocks the cystic duct, stopping bile from flowing out of the gallbladder. [learn more](BMP125_U4_T4#BMP125_U4_T4_h1)

question: What is the main goal of routine urine testing during early pregnancy antenatal visits?

options.A: To measure daily food and nutrient intake
options.B: To confirm the exact age of the pregnancy
options.C: To check for underlying gestational diabetes
options.D: To find and treat silent bacteria in the urine before they turn into a kidney infection

explanation: Screening catches hidden bladder infections early so they can be treated before bacteria travel up to cause severe kidney infections. [learn more](BMP216_U1_T2#BMP216_U1_T2_h7)

question: Which hormone drops to almost zero because ovulation and corpus luteum formation stop?

options.A: Estrogen
options.B: Progesterone
options.C: Prolactin
options.D: Oxytocin

explanation: Progesterone is mainly made by the corpus luteum after ovulation, so cycles without ovulation mean progesterone production stops. [learn more](BMP320_U1_T1#BMP320_U1_T1_h3)

question: How does untreated iodine deficiency in pregnancy affect a newborn's future learning potential?

options.A: It accelerates brain growth so much that the child develops severe headaches
options.B: It permanently prevents the child from learning to speak any language
options.C: It can lower intelligence quotient and cause learning difficulties in school
options.D: It causes severe blindness and hearing loss within the first year of life

explanation: Not having enough thyroid hormone during key brain development windows limits neural pathways, which can affect learning later in childhood. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T5#BMP118_U4_T5_h5)

question: What does the letter 'S' stand for in the SBAR handover tool?

options.A: Salary
options.B: Schedule
options.C: Supplies
options.D: Situation

explanation: In SBAR, the first step is stating the current Situation clearly. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T1#BMP324_U1_T1_h4)

question: Why is the structure of the alveolar membrane ideal for gas exchange in the lungs?

options.A: It contains thick layers of muscle to push gases along
options.B: It uses active transport pumps to pull oxygen inward
options.C: It blocks carbon dioxide from ever leaving the blood
options.D: It is extremely thin and provides a large surface area

explanation: A large surface area and minimal thickness create optimal conditions for rapid gas diffusion between the lungs and blood. [learn more](BMP111_U1_T3#BMP111_U1_T3_h6)

question: Why is Sulfadoxine-Pyrimethamine used for intermittent preventive treatment instead of other antimalarial drugs?

options.A: It acts as a strong pain reliever for pregnancy-related joint aches
options.B: It completely cures all strains of resistant bacteria in the blood
options.C: It stimulates the rapid production of red blood cells in the bone marrow
options.D: It is safe for routine prophylactic dosing during pregnancy and effective

explanation: SP has a favorable safety profile for continuous intermittent use during the second and third trimesters to clear subclinical parasitaemia. [learn more](BMP221_U4_T5#BMP221_U4_T5_h4)

question: What is the main job of a negative feedback loop in the endocrine system?

options.A: To reverse a change and restore normal balance
options.B: To turn chemical signals into fast electrical impulses
options.C: To permanently stop hormone production in all glands
options.D: To amplify a stimulus until a physical event finishes

explanation: Negative feedback works by counteracting a change, bringing the internal environment back to its normal baseline. [learn more](BMP121_U4_T3#BMP121_U4_T3_h2)

question: Why is routine deworming recommended during the second trimester in endemic areas?

options.A: To cure severe morning sickness and vomiting
options.B: To stop the baby from swallowing meconium
options.C: To clear out dangerous tapeworms from the lungs
options.D: To prevent chronic blood loss from hookworms

explanation: Hookworms attach to the intestinal wall and feed on blood, causing silent chronic blood loss that worsens maternal anemia. [learn more](BMP221_U4_T1#BMP221_U4_T1_h5)

question: Why is strict confidentiality especially crucial when managing maternal mental health issues?

options.A: It prevents family members from ever visiting the postnatal ward
options.B: It stops nurses from communicating with each other during shift handovers
options.C: Hospital management requires all mental health records to be published publicly
options.D: Stigma surrounding mental illness in many communities can deter women from seeking care

explanation: Fear of judgment or gossip stops many mothers from speaking up, so guarding their privacy protects their willingness to seek help. [learn more](BMP223_U4_T6#BMP223_U4_T6_h6)

question: What is the most common reason patients stop taking erythromycin early?

options.A: Sudden total hair loss across the scalp
options.B: Severe permanent blindness
options.C: Stomach upset like nausea and cramping
options.D: Uncontrollable muscle spasms in the legs

explanation: Stomach irritation and cramping often cause patients to stop taking erythromycin before finishing the course. [learn more](BMP124_U4_T4#BMP124_U4_T4_h5)

question: What size of intravenous cannula is best for emergency access during a major hemorrhage?

options.A: Small-bore 22 gauge
options.B: Central line 24 gauge
options.C: Standard 20 gauge
options.D: Large-bore 16 or 14 gauge

explanation: Large-bore cannulas allow rapid fluid and blood replacement, which is critical when managing hypovolaemic shock. [learn more](BMP221_U2_T4#BMP221_U2_T4_h3)

question: What defines transient hand flora?

options.A: Harmless microbes that naturally protect skin
options.B: Bacteria that live permanently deep under the skin
options.C: Microbes that multiply without oxygen
options.D: Organisms picked up from touching contaminated surfaces or patients

explanation: Transient flora are picked up during daily tasks and are easily removed by proper hand hygiene. [learn more](BMP110_U5_T11#BMP110_U5_T11_h3)

question: What is the main function of the vent pipe in a Ventilated Improved Pit latrine?

options.A: Drain rainwater away from the toilet seat
options.B: Control odors and trap flying insects
options.C: Supply fresh air for people using the facility
options.D: Allow users to clean the pit from outside

explanation: The screened vent pipe draws bad smells upward and catches flies trying to escape the pit, breaking the disease transmission cycle. [learn more](BMP117_U4_T2#BMP117_U4_T2_h3)

question: Why is pregnancy tough on a woman who needs heart medications?

options.A: Red blood cell destruction accelerates rapidly in the third trimester
options.B: Blood volume increases by up to fifty percent, raising cardiac workload
options.C: The placenta produces hormones that directly block cardiac receptors
options.D: Pregnancy causes the heart muscle to shrink significantly in size

explanation: A pregnant woman's body carries much more blood, which forces a weak heart to work harder to keep up. [learn more](BMP213_U3_T7#BMP213_U3_T7_h1)

question: How does the lymphatic system differ mainly from the blood circulation system?

options.A: A high-pressure pumping network powered directly by the heart
options.B: A closed-loop system carrying oxygenated blood to all deep tissues
options.C: A solid structural barrier preventing any fluid movement between tissues
options.D: A low-pressure drainage network that collects excess interstitial fluid

explanation: The lymphatic system works as a low-pressure drainage network to gather fluid that escapes from blood capillaries into body tissues. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T1#BMP111_U6_T1_h1)

question: Why is direct communication with the receiving facility essential during a patient referral?

options.A: To cancel all previous diagnostic lab test results
options.B: To allow the transferring midwife to negotiate treatment costs
options.C: To transfer legal ownership of the patient's personal property
options.D: To ensure the receiving team expects the patient and prepares necessary resources

explanation: Calling ahead alerts the destination team so they can ready the labor room, blood bank, or specialists before the patient arrives. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T7#BMP110_U2_T7_h4)

question: What substance normally helps prevent kidney stones from forming in the urine?

options.A: Citrate
options.B: Sodium chloride
options.C: Calcium oxalate
options.D: Uric acid

explanation: Citrate acts as a natural inhibitor in the urine that stops crystals from clumping together to form stones. [learn more](BMP216_U1_T10#BMP216_U1_T10_h1)

question: A pregnant woman at twenty-four weeks gestation visits the clinic complaining only of persistent tiredness and mild dizziness. What is the most appropriate initial action?

options.A: Perform a malaria test despite the lack of high fever
options.B: Send her home to rest since dizziness is common
options.C: Admit her immediately for intravenous fluid therapy
options.D: Prescribe heavy iron supplements for normal fatigue

explanation: Semi-immune pregnant women may present with quiet symptoms like fatigue instead of classic high fevers, making diagnostic testing essential. [learn more](BMP221_U4_T5#BMP221_U4_T5_h3)

question: What is the term for the process where rhythmic muscle contractions in the pelvis expel semen?

options.A: Micturition
options.B: Peristalsis
options.C: Ejaculation
options.D: Erection

explanation: Ejaculation is the expulsion of semen driven by coordinated muscular contractions in the pelvic region. [learn more](BMP210_U3_T1#BMP210_U3_T1_h3)

question: What infant feeding practice is recommended for mothers on ART with a suppressed viral load in Nigeria?

options.A: Exclusive breastfeeding for the first six months
options.B: Mixed feeding with breast milk and water from birth
options.C: Immediate formula feeding from day one after birth
options.D: Early introduction of solid family foods at two months

explanation: Exclusive breastfeeding combined with maternal ART provides the best health outcomes while minimizing the risk of HIV transmission. [learn more](BMP213_U4_T6#BMP213_U4_T6_h5)

question: Why must sexual partners be treated along with the patient for chlamydia?

options.A: It prevents the bacteria from mutating into a virus.
options.B: It strengthens the patient's long-term immunity.
options.C: It cures the primary patient's chronic headaches.
options.D: It stops the cycle of reinfection between partners.

explanation: If sexual partners are not treated at the same time, they will continuously pass the infection back and forth. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T5#BMP310_U2_T5_h5)

question: What main factor often increases a person's vulnerability upon admission to a health institution?

options.A: Immediate appointment to a leadership board
options.B: Complete freedom to direct hospital schedules
options.C: Excessive availability of home-cooked meals
options.D: Loss of personal control and unfamiliar routines

explanation: Hospital admission places individuals into strict institutional routines, reducing their autonomy and increasing vulnerability. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T5#BMP110_U2_T5_h3)

question: What is the very first step of the nursing process in clinical practice?

options.A: Planning
options.B: Evaluation
options.C: Assessment
options.D: Diagnosis

explanation: Assessment forms the foundational first step upon which all other nursing actions depend. [learn more](BMP120_U1_T2#BMP120_U1_T2_h1)

question: What structures directly control the entry of blood into true capillary networks?

options.A: Venous pumps
options.B: Endothelial flaps
options.C: Arterial valves
options.D: Precapillary sphincters

explanation: Precapillary sphincters are rings of smooth muscle that open and close to direct blood flow into the capillary beds as needed. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T15#BMP111_U5_T15_h3)

question: What type of error happens when data is consistently pushed in one direction due to a repeatable bias?

options.A: Transcription error
options.B: Random error
options.C: Systematic error
options.D: Sampling error

explanation: Systematic errors occur consistently due to flawed tools or procedures, skewing the study results in a specific direction. [learn more](BMP225_U3_T3#BMP225_U3_T3_h2)

question: Which quality is essential for a democratic healthcare leader?

options.A: Active listening
options.B: Secretive planning
options.C: Ignoring feedback
options.D: Strict isolation

explanation: Active listening helps a democratic leader truly hear and value what the clinical team has to say. [learn more](BMP312_U1_T9#BMP312_U1_T9_h2)

question: Why are regular audits helpful for a busy maternity ward?

options.A: They uncover inefficiencies, prevent theft, and ensure policy compliance
options.B: They automatically increase the annual government health budget
options.C: They replace the daily nursing handover process
options.D: They eliminate the need for midwives to document patient care

explanation: Audits provide a systematic check that discourages financial dishonesty and highlights where resources are leaking. [learn more](BMP312_U2_T3#BMP312_U2_T3_h4)

question: Which term describes measuring the intensity of care a patient needs based on their clinical condition?

options.A: Roster rotation
options.B: Inventory auditing
options.C: Patient acuity
options.D: Bed occupancy

explanation: Patient acuity looks at how sick a patient is and how much hands-on care they require from the midwifery staff. [learn more](BMP312_U2_T1#BMP312_U2_T1_h2)

question: Why can't Trichomonas vaginalis survive for a long time outside the human body?

options.A: It lacks a resistant cyst stage in its life cycle
options.B: It requires human body temperature to replicate its DNA
options.C: It depends entirely on dietary iron found only in blood
options.D: It is quickly destroyed by high levels of environmental oxygen

explanation: Without a tough outer shell or cyst stage to protect it, the parasite quickly dies when exposed to the outside environment. [learn more](BMP116_U3_T6#BMP116_U3_T6_h1)

question: Who should a midwife contact immediately after a major cold chain failure at a primary health post?

options.A: The local police division headquarters
options.B: The Local Government Immunisation Officer (LIO)
options.C: The vaccine manufacturing company abroad
options.D: The national electricity distribution company

explanation: The LIO coordinates district logistics, helps arrange emergency replacement stock, and dispatches technicians. [learn more](BMP117_U3_T4#BMP117_U3_T4_h6)

question: A patient having labor induced with misoprostol develops six contractions in ten minutes, and the fetal monitor shows late decelerations. What is the midwife's first action?

options.A: Document the findings and wait another thirty minutes to see if it stops
options.B: Turn the patient to her left side and apply oxygen
options.C: Administer a dose of synthetic oxytocin to regularize the rhythm
options.D: Encourage the woman to push hard with the next contraction

explanation: Helping the mother lie on her side and giving oxygen improves blood flow to the placenta and helps relieve stress on the baby during too many contractions. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T8#BMP213_U1_T8_h8)

question: Why is acid-alcohol used in the Ziehl-Neelsen staining procedure?

options.A: To kill all live bacteria before the slide is looked at
options.B: To wash the red stain out of non-acid-fast cells
options.C: To act as the primary dye that colors the bacterial wall
options.D: To fix the clinical sample firmly onto the glass slide

explanation: Acid-alcohol strips the red carbolfuchsin dye away from ordinary cells, while acid-fast bacteria hold onto the color because of their waxy walls. [learn more](BMP116_U1_T3#BMP116_U1_T3_h5)

question: Why is heparin generally avoided during acute obstetric DIC when bleeding is already widespread?

options.A: It causes severe allergic reactions in postpartum women
options.B: It prevents further clotting when the patient is already at high risk of hemorrhaging
options.C: It immediately destroys all remaining red blood cells in the circulation
options.D: It permanently stops the kidneys from producing urine

explanation: Since the patient is already bleeding uncontrollably from a lack of clotting factors, giving an anti-clotting medication like heparin would worsen the hemorrhage. [learn more](BMP311_U4_T6#BMP311_U4_T6_h6)

question: A patient is due for her magnesium sulfate maintenance dose, but her breathing rate is 10 breaths per minute. What should the midwife do?

options.A: Proceed with the injection because seizures are worse
options.B: Withhold the dose and report to the doctor immediately
options.C: Give half the normal maintenance dose to be safe
options.D: Administer a dose of oral calcium gluconate right away

explanation: A breathing rate under 16 breaths per minute is a sign of magnesium toxicity. The dose must be held and the doctor called. [learn more](BMP315_U2_T1#BMP315_U2_T1_h5)

question: What is a key trait that helps a shift coordinator build good team morale?

options.A: Assigning yourself the easiest tasks every single day
options.B: Transparent duty rosters and fair work distribution
options.C: Refusing to listen to complaints from junior staff
options.D: Keeping all clinical information a secret from juniors

explanation: Fairness in scheduling stops staff from feeling cheated and keeps the working environment cooperative. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T1#BMP324_U1_T1_h3)

question: What is the first critical action a midwife must take if an umbilical cord prolapses?

options.A: Administer oxytocin infusion to speed up the normal vaginal delivery
options.B: Manually push the presenting part upward to relieve pressure off the cord
options.C: Instruct the mother to stand up and walk around to reposition the baby
options.D: Wait patiently for natural cervical dilation to complete on its own

explanation: Relieving pressure on the prolapsed cord by elevating the fetal part is the single most important step to prevent oxygen loss while preparing for delivery. [learn more](BMP210_U5_T3#BMP210_U5_T3_h6)

question: Which practice helps ensure files are easily sorted in chronological order within a folder?

options.A: Writing file names in lowercase letters only
options.B: Using only random numbers as file titles
options.C: Including dates clearly in the file names
options.D: Keeping all documents saved on the desktop screen

explanation: Starting file names with dates (such as year and month) causes the operating system to arrange them neatly in order of creation time. [learn more](BMP123_U2_T3#BMP123_U2_T3_h6)

question: What is the primary clinical use of Mid-Upper Arm Circumference (MUAC) measurement in midwifery care?

options.A: Calculating precise fetal birth weight
options.B: Screening for acute malnutrition
options.C: Estimating maternal blood volume
options.D: Diagnosing gestational diabetes mellitus

explanation: MUAC provides a quick, reliable indicator of nutritional status and muscle wasting, especially in community settings. [learn more](BMP110_U6_T3#BMP110_U6_T3_h5)

question: What characterizes the bargaining stage of grief?

options.A: Blaming family members for the event
options.B: Accepting reality without emotional pain
options.C: Experiencing complete physical numbness
options.D: Making secret deals or promises to reverse the loss

explanation: Bargaining involves trying to negotiate with fate or a higher power to change an outcome that has already occurred. [learn more](BMP120_U5_T3#BMP120_U5_T3_h4)

question: What is the primary goal of admitting a patient to the high-risk antenatal ward?

options.A: Ensuring immediate delivery within twenty-four hours
options.B: Providing intensive surveillance and timely intervention
options.C: Conducting routine screening for low-risk women
options.D: Preparing the patient for permanent family planning

explanation: High-risk wards focus heavily on close monitoring and quick action to catch complications early before they harm mother or baby. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T1#BMP315_U1_T1_h1)

question: Which mineral is especially critical for preventing anemia in women of reproductive age?

options.A: Sodium
options.B: Iron
options.C: Potassium
options.D: Calcium

explanation: Iron is a core component of hemoglobin, which carries oxygen in the red blood cells, replacing losses from menstruation. [learn more](BMP118_U3_T6#BMP118_U3_T6_h3)

question: Why is it important for midwives to address the emotional side of morning sickness?

options.A: Emotional stress directly stops the placenta from making hormones
options.B: Counseling replaces the need for any dietary changes at home
options.C: Prolonged nausea can lead to anxiety, guilt, and emotional distress
options.D: Mental upset is the single leading cause of hyperemesis gravidarum

explanation: Feeling sick constantly drains a mother emotionally, making empathetic counseling essential to help her cope with the psychological burden. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T10#BMP212_U1_T10_h6)

question: What happens to passive antibodies in the human body over time?

options.A: They are gradually broken down and cleared from circulation
options.B: They bind permanently to host tissues and remain there forever
options.C: They transform into active memory cells to fight future infections
options.D: They multiply inside the bone marrow to form a permanent reserve

explanation: The body treats introduced antibodies like any other circulating protein, breaking them down over several weeks or months. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T8#BMP111_U6_T8_h4)

question: A new mother with a history of psychosis is going home. Which action by the midwife best supports her care?

options.A: Encouraging her to isolate herself to reduce environmental stress
options.B: Scheduling early postpartum mental health check-ins and support
options.C: Discontinuing all physical health monitoring once she leaves the hospital
